questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Inferior gluteal nerve as a branch of the sacral plexus
questions.question: Which one of the following nerves is a branch of the sacral plexus?

options.D: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh.

explanations.A: Correct. The inferior gluteal nerve arises from the sacral plexus, carrying fibres from L5, S1 and S2. It leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below the piriformis. It then supplies the gluteus maximus, the main extensor of the hip.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The femoral nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus (L2-L4).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The obturator nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus (L2-L4).
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh arises from the lumbar plexus (L2-L3).

questions.learning_objective: Identify the inferior gluteal nerve as a sacral plexus branch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q3 = a)

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Deep artery of the penis as a branch of the internal pudendal artery
questions.question: Which one of the following arteries is a branch of the internal pudendal artery?

explanations.A: Correct. The internal pudendal artery is the chief artery of the perineum. After giving its inferior rectal and perineal branches it ends by supplying the erectile tissue. Its terminal branches are the artery of the bulb, the dorsal artery of the penis and the deep artery of the penis, the last running within the corpus cavernosum.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Medial sacral' is not a named branch here; the midline sacral vessel is the median sacral artery, which arises from the abdominal aorta, not the internal pudendal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The median sacral artery arises from the back of the abdominal aorta just above its bifurcation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The superior rectal artery is the continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the deep artery of the penis as a branch of the internal pudendal artery.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q4 = a)

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Arterial supply of the ureter from the gonadal artery
questions.question: Which one of the following arteries gives a blood supply to the ureter?

explanations.A: Correct. The ureter has a segmental blood supply along its whole length. In the abdomen it receives constant branches from the renal and the gonadal (testicular or ovarian) arteries, and in the pelvis from the vesical and uterine arteries. Of the options offered, only the gonadal artery is a recognised ureteric supplier.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The superior vesical artery supplies mainly the upper bladder; it is not the recognised principal ureteric supplier among these options (the lower ureter is supplied more by the inferior vesical/uterine arteries).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut, not the ureter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The external iliac artery gives no branch to the ureter; it supplies the lower limb (its branches are the inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries).

questions.learning_objective: State that the gonadal (testicular/ovarian) artery contributes to the ureteric blood supply.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Deep transverse perineal muscle as a content of the deep perineal pouch
questions.question: The deep perineal pouch in the female contains which one of the following?

explanations.B: Correct. The deep perineal pouch lies between the perineal membrane below and the pelvic diaphragm above. It contains the deep transverse perineal muscle and the sphincter urethrae. It also transmits the internal pudendal vessels and the dorsal nerve of the clitoris.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The ischiocavernosus lies in the superficial perineal pouch.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands lie in the superficial perineal pouch in the female.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The bulb of the vestibule lies in the superficial perineal pouch.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the deep transverse perineal muscle as a content of the deep perineal pouch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q12 = b)

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Ischiocavernosus lies in the superficial perineal pouch
questions.question: The ischiocavernosus muscle is found in the:

explanations.B: Correct. The superficial perineal pouch lies between the perineal membrane and the deep perineal fascia. Its three paired muscles are the ischiocavernosus, the bulbospongiosus and the superficial transverse perineal muscle. The ischiocavernosus covers the crus of the penis or clitoris and helps to maintain erection.
explanations.A: Incorrect. It is a perineal, not a true-pelvic, muscle; it lies below the pelvic diaphragm.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The deep perineal pouch contains the deep transverse perineal muscle and sphincter urethrae, not the ischiocavernosus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ischiorectal fossa is a fat-filled space lateral to the anal canal; the ischiocavernosus is not one of its contents.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the ischiocavernosus in the superficial perineal pouch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q15 = b)

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands in the superficial perineal pouch
questions.question: Which one of the following structures is present in the superficial perineal pouch in the female?

explanations.C: Correct. In the female the superficial perineal pouch holds the crura and bulbs of the erectile tissue with their muscles. Behind the bulbs of the vestibule lie the greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands. These glands are therefore contents of the superficial, not the deep, perineal pouch.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The sphincter urethrae lies in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The deep transverse perineal muscle lies in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The bulbourethral glands are the male homologue and lie in the deep perineal pouch in the male; they are not present in the female.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the greater vestibular glands in the female superficial perineal pouch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q25 = c)

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Ejaculate composition after vasectomy
questions.question: Two months after a vasectomy in which the ductus deferens was ligated in the upper part of the scrotum, the ejaculate contains:

explanations.B: Correct. Vasectomy divides the ductus deferens, so sperm can no longer reach the ejaculate. The secretions added downstream of the cut, from the seminal vesicles and the prostate, still enter the urethra normally. The ejaculate therefore contains seminal and prostatic fluids but no sperm.
explanations.A: Incorrect. Prostatic fluid is present, but so is the seminal vesicle secretion, which forms the largest volume fraction of semen, so 'prostatic only' is wrong.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sperm are exactly what is lost once the ductus deferens is divided.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sperm are absent after vasectomy; seminal fluid remains along with prostatic fluid.

questions.learning_objective: Predict the composition of the ejaculate after vasectomy.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q16 = b)

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Penile urethra lies within the corpus spongiosum
questions.question: In the male, the penile (spongy) part of the urethra is the part that:

options.B: Starts at the trigone of the bladder.

explanations.D: Correct. The male urethra has prostatic, membranous and spongy (penile) parts. The spongy part is the longest and runs the whole length of the corpus spongiosum of the penis. It is therefore the part that lies within the corpus spongiosum.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The part within the prostate is the prostatic urethra.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The urethra begins at the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck, not at the trigone (a region of the bladder wall).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The part traversing the urogenital diaphragm is the membranous urethra.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the spongy urethra as the part within the corpus spongiosum.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The anterior lobe of the prostate is devoid of glandular tissue
questions.question: Regarding the prostate, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Its anterior lobe is devoid of glandular tissue.
options.B: Its anterior lobe is rich in glandular tissue.
options.C: Its posterior surface is related to the levator ani muscles.
options.D: The prostatic venous plexus drains into the external iliac vein.

explanations.A: Correct. The prostate is described in lobes arranged around the urethra and ejaculatory ducts. The anterior lobe (isthmus), lying in front of the urethra, is composed of fibromuscular tissue. It is essentially devoid of glandular acini, so it is rarely a site of disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This is the reverse of the truth; the anterior lobe contains little or no glandular tissue.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The posterior surface is related to the ampulla of the rectum; the levator ani lies laterally as the levator prostatae.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins and the vertebral venous plexus, not the external iliac vein.

questions.learning_objective: State that the anterior lobe of the prostate lacks glandular tissue.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The posterior surface of the prostate is related to the ampulla of the rectum
questions.question: Regarding the prostate, choose the correct statement:

options.A: Its base is continuous with the apex of the bladder.
options.B: Its posterior surface is related to the ampulla of the rectum.
options.C: Benign enlargement commonly involves the posterior lobe.
options.D: The prostatic venous plexus drains into the external iliac veins.

explanations.B: Correct. The prostate sits below the bladder with its base above and apex below. Its posterior surface is separated from the ampulla of the rectum only by the rectovesical fascia of Denonvilliers. This is why the gland is palpable through the anterior rectal wall on digital rectal examination.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The base is continuous with the neck, not the apex, of the bladder.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Benign hyperplasia arises in the median/transitional (periurethral) zone; the posterior lobe is the common site of carcinoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins and the vertebral plexus, not the external iliac veins.

questions.learning_objective: Relate the posterior surface of the prostate to the rectal ampulla.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q38 = b)

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The base of the prostate is continuous with the neck of the bladder
questions.question: Regarding the prostate gland, choose the correct statement:

options.A: Its base is continuous with the neck of the urinary bladder.
options.B: Its anterior surface is related to the ampulla of the rectum.
options.C: The ejaculatory ducts open on to the anterior wall of the prostatic urethra.
options.D: The prostatic venous plexus drains into the external iliac veins.

explanations.A: Correct. The prostate is shaped like an inverted cone with the base directed upward. The base is directly continuous with the neck of the urinary bladder, through which the urethra passes. Its apex rests below on the sphincter urethrae in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.B: Incorrect. It is the posterior, not the anterior, surface that is related to the ampulla of the rectum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The ejaculatory ducts open on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra, on the seminal colliculus beside the prostatic utricle.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic venous plexus drains into the internal iliac veins and the vertebral plexus.

questions.learning_objective: State that the base of the prostate is continuous with the bladder neck.

questions.subject: gi
questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the anal canal below the pectinate line
questions.question: Lymphatic vessels from the anal canal below the pectinate line drain into which lymph nodes?

explanations.D: Correct. The pectinate (dentate) line marks the junction of the endodermal and ectodermal parts of the anal canal. Below the line the lining is somatic (ectodermal), so its lymph drains to the superficial inguinal nodes. Above the line the visceral part drains upward to the internal iliac and inferior mesenteric nodes.
explanations.A: Incorrect. Para-aortic nodes drain the gonads and kidneys, not the lower anal canal.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Superior mesenteric nodes drain the midgut.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Internal iliac nodes drain the anal canal above the pectinate line, not below it.

questions.learning_objective: State the inguinal lymph drainage of the anal canal below the pectinate line.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q14 = d)

questions.subject: gi
questions.title: Lymphatic drainage of the rectum
questions.question: Lymph vessels of the rectum drain into which one of the following groups of lymph nodes?

explanations.B: Correct. Rectal lymph follows the arteries that supply the rectum. Along the superior rectal vessels it passes to the inferior mesenteric nodes, and along the middle rectal vessels to the internal iliac nodes. Its drainage is therefore to the inferior mesenteric and internal iliac groups.
explanations.A: Incorrect. Superior mesenteric nodes drain the midgut, not the rectum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. External iliac nodes drain the lower limb and viscera such as the bladder, not the rectum.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Inguinal nodes drain the anal canal below the pectinate line and the lower limb, not the rectum.

questions.learning_objective: State the lymphatic drainage of the rectum.

questions.subject: gi
questions.title: Nature of external haemorrhoids
questions.question: External haemorrhoids are:

options.A: Varicosities of tributaries of the superior rectal veins covered with mucous membrane.
options.B: Varicosities of tributaries of the inferior rectal veins covered with skin.
options.C: A tear in the anal valves extending down to the anus.
options.D: An abscess in the submucosa of the anal canal.

explanations.B: Correct. External haemorrhoids arise below the pectinate line, in the territory of the inferior rectal veins. Because this part of the anal canal is lined by skin, they are covered by skin and are sensitive to pain. Internal haemorrhoids, by contrast, are dilatations of the superior rectal (portal) tributaries above the line, covered by mucous membrane.
explanations.A: Incorrect. That description (superior rectal tributaries, mucous membrane) is an internal haemorrhoid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A tear in the anal lining is an anal fissure, not a haemorrhoid.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A submucosal collection of pus is an anal abscess, not a haemorrhoid.

questions.learning_objective: Define external haemorrhoids and distinguish them from internal haemorrhoids.
